claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 3 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 3 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**How many children do you want to check for Child Benefit eligibility?** And could you tell me:

1. **Their name(s)**
2. **Their age(s)** - This is important as the rules differ depending on whether they're under 16, 16-19, or 20 and over

Once I have this information, I can walk you through the eligibility checks for each child.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who is 3 years old. We live together here in Birmingham, and I just want to make sure I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! That's helpful context. So you have one child, **Alex, who is 3 years old** - that's great because at 3 years old, Alex is under 16, which means they automatically qualify as a "qualifying child" for Child Benefit purposes.

Now I need to check a few more things to determine your overall eligibility. Let me continue through the assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

(Since Alex is 3 years old, this is likely "yes" - I'm just checking this for completeness!)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex doesn't work at all. They're only 3, so they're not in any kind of paid work.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Since Alex is only 3 years old and not in paid work, we can move on to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

(Again, at 3 years old, this is likely "yes", but I need to confirm this.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name. They're just a toddler, so nothing like that applies to them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear. Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in any kind of apprenticeship?**

(At 3 years old, this is almost certainly "no" - but I need to confirm for the assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship. They're only 3 years old - far too young for anything like that!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Absolutely! That makes perfect sense. Let me move forward:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now we need to check your residency status. You mentioned you live in Birmingham, which is in England. Let me ask about your residency situation to ensure you meet the requirements:

**Which of the following best describes your residency status?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this would apply to you since you're in Birmingham)
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** (and if so, which situation applies - working, seeking work, studying, etc.)
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad**

Since you've mentioned living in Birmingham, I'm guessing the first option applies - that you normally live in the UK. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - I normally live in the UK. We're based here in Birmingham, and this is our home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That confirms you meet the residency requirements. Let me move forward:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex. There are a few ways you could be considered responsible:

1. **You live with the child** (this applies if Alex lives with you)
2. **You contribute to the child's upkeep** - this means paying at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards their care (including things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents)
3. **You're paying maintenance** under a court order or agreement

**Do any of these apply to you? Specifically, do you live with Alex and contribute to their care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me here at home. We live together, so I'm the one looking after them day to day.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear - you live with Alex and are responsible for their day-to-day care. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check an important question: **Is there anyone else also claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or would anyone else potentially be eligible to claim?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent also claiming or could they claim?
- Is another family member claiming for Alex?

Or is it just you making a claim for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, it's just me. Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex - I'm the only one looking to claim it.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's straightforward - there's no dispute about who's claiming. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation. **Is Alex:**

1. **In hospital** (for longer periods)
2. **In care** (such as local authority care)
3. **Fostered** (with foster carers)
4. **Living normally at home** with you

Based on what you've told me so far, I assume Alex is living normally at home with you - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex is living normally at home with me. They're not in hospital, care, or fostered or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! One final check: **Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you fully responsible for supporting Alex yourself, rather than the council paying for their care or accommodation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. I'm supporting them myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's all the information I need. Let me now provide you with the final outcome:

reasonings: Alex is 3 years old, which means they are under 16 and automatically qualify as a qualifying child. Alex is not in paid work, does not receive any benefits in their own right, and is not in an apprenticeship. You normally live in the UK (Birmingham), which meets the residency requirements. You live with Alex and are responsible for their day-to-day care. There is no other claimant for Child Benefit for Alex. Alex is living normally at home with you (not in hospital, care, or foster care). The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. All eligibility criteria have been met.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Alex meets all the qualifying criteria: they are under 16, you have responsibility for them by living with them, you meet residency requirements, there are no conflicting claimants, and the local council is not providing financial support. You can proceed to make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex.">
